chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir from 'Umar ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) set the Miqat for the people of the East as Al-'Aqiq, approximately two post-stages, between the post-stage of Al-Ba'ath and Ghumrah. And he set for the people of Medina Dhu al-Hulayfah, and for the people of Najd Qarn al-Manazil, and for the people of Syria Al-Juhfah, and for the people of Yemen Yalamlam.

key_terms.ذُو الْحُلَيْفَةِ: Dhu al-Hulayfah (Miqat for people of Medina)
key_terms.غَمْرَةَ: Ghumrah (a place near Mecca, often associated with a Miqat or prayer spot)
key_terms.قَرْنَ الْمَنَازِلِ: Qarn al-Manazil (Miqat for people of Najd)

ai.seo_question: What are the designated Miqat stations for pilgrims from different regions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* codifies the Miqat stations, establishing a structured framework for the Hajj pilgrimage that reflects the geographical and administrative divisions of the early Islamic world. It highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) role in standardizing ritual boundaries, ensuring uniformity in the commencement of Ihram for pilgrims from diverse regions such as Medina, Najd, and Syria. This legal precision underscores the importance of order and intentionality in Islamic worship, a theme central to Shia jurisprudence.
